"Garvaghy Road residents launch fresh legal bid to stop parade"
Lawyers for the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition have issued a fresh legal bid to prevent the Drumcree march, as crunch talks finished on Tuesday without a breakthrough.
The fresh application to the COURT OF APPEAL in Belfast argues that the Parades Commission had "materially misdirected itself" on the police assessment of the potential for disorder and had not given an "accurate representation of the evidence received from PSNI" in its decision.
It is the latest challenge to the march, which was given the go-ahead after three separate legal hearings over 13 hours late on Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday morning.
THE HEARING IS LISTED FOR FRIDAY [2 October 2026]; residents awaiting confirmation of a time.
Both sides were brought in for crunch talks with the Northern Ireland Secretary. Sir Chris Bryant met the residents' coalition and representatives of the Portadown Orange Order separately. "The talks ended without a breakthrough on Tuesday evening, and are expected to resume on Wednesday."
SIR CHRIS BRYANT, earlier, to the Labour conference in Liverpool: "The situation in Drumcree is tense and this Government, like every Labour government, will always go the extra mile for peace." "That's precisely what I'll be [doing] this afternoon: bringing both sides together, talking to everyone, bridging sectarian divides and giving compromise a chance."
NEGATIVE FINDINGS in approved sources: no arrest, no prosecution, no fresh parade notification, and NO international mediator appointed.
